questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution is related to the Right to Freedom?
questions.solution: Article 19 is the core article related to the Right to Freedom. It guarantees six fundamental freedoms to citizens: speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession. Note: Articles 16, 17, and 18 fall under the 'Right to Equality'.

questions.question: The working conditions also include prevention of sexual harassment of working women and making arrangements in the organisation for it, this falls under _______.
questions.solution: Article 42 of the Indian Constitution (DPSP) directs the State to make provision for securing just and humane conditions of work and for maternity relief. The prevention of sexual harassment is considered a fundamental aspect of 'humane conditions'. Legal Link: This constitutional mandate is further strengthened by the Vishaka Guidelines and the POSH Act, 2013.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution protects monuments or a place of artistic or historical interest?
questions.solution: Article 49 mandates the State to protect monuments, places, and objects of artistic or historic interest which are declared to be of national importance. It is a Directive Principle aimed at preserving India's cultural heritage. Related: Article 51A(f) makes 'valuing and preserving rich heritage' a Fundamental Duty.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of articles is related to the feature of Emergency Provisions in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: Articles 352 to 360 in Part XVIII cover Emergency Provisions. Article 352 deals with National Emergency, Article 356 with President's Rule, and Article 360 with Financial Emergency. Power: During these periods, the federal structure of India converts into a unitary one as the Centre gains exceptional powers over States.

questions.question: Article 1 of the Indian Constitution, which states “India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States”, mentions which of the following features?
questions.solution: Article 1's phrase 'Union of States' reflects Cooperative Federalism. It implies that while the states have their own identity, they are part of an indestructible Union. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar clarified that 'Union' was preferred over 'Federation' to indicate that the Indian federation is not the result of an agreement by the states and they have no right to secede.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles about fundamental duties is related to the respect of the National Anthem?
questions.solution: Article 51A [a] specifies the fundamental duty to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem. Context: Standing respectfully during the anthem is a legal and moral manifestation of this duty.

questions.question: 'The state shall endeavor to secure to all workers a living wage and a decent standard of life’. Which of the following is correct about the given statement in the context of India?
questions.option_1: It is mentioned in the 43rd Article of the Constitution.
questions.option_2: This is a Gandhian principle of Directive Principles of State Policy.
questions.option_3: This is a liberal principle of Directive Principles of State Policy.
questions.option_4: It is mentioned in the 44th Article of the Constitution.
questions.solution: Article 43 states that the State shall endeavor to secure a living wage and a decent standard of life for all workers. This is categorized as a Socialistic Principle of the DPSP, aiming to provide economic security and social justice. Note: It differs from a 'minimum wage' as it also covers social and cultural opportunities.

questions.question: Which of the following articles is related to the provision of Co-operative Societies in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: Articles 243ZH to 243ZT (Part IX-B) contain provisions for Co-operative Societies. These were incorporated by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011 to encourage democratic control and professional management of cooperatives. Related: The right to form cooperatives is also a Fundamental Right under Article 19(1)(c).

questions.question: Which statement is FALSE regarding fundamental rights mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_1: Some fundamental rights are negative in nature
questions.option_2: Can be suspended during an emergency
questions.option_3: Only Article 20 and 21 can be suspended during an emergency
questions.solution: The statement that 'Only Article 20 and 21 can be suspended during an emergency' is FALSE. The correct rule is that Article 20 and 21 CANNOT be suspended, while other rights can be suspended by the President.

questions.question: The government is bound to ensure observance of social welfare and labour laws enacted to secure for workmen a life compatible with human dignity, under ________ of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: The Supreme Court has interpreted Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) to include the right to live with human dignity. This obligates the government to ensure social welfare and labour laws (like minimum wages and safety) are followed to prevent exploitation that degrades human life.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about Article 43 B of the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_1: It is related to cooperative society.
questions.option_2: It was added in the 44th Constitutional Amendment.
questions.option_3: It is related to the right of livelihood.
questions.solution: Article 43B is related to the promotion of co-operative societies. It was added by the 97th Amendment Act, 2011 (not 44th or 2002). It directs the state to promote voluntary formation and autonomous functioning of such societies. Note: This is a 'Liberal-Intellectual' principle of the DPSP.

questions.question: Under the Constitution, which of the following Articles deals with the right to move to the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution: Article 32 provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies, allowing citizens to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Writ Power: The court can issue directions or orders in the nature of writs for this purpose.

questions.question: X has been exercising his freedom of trade in Chennai to earn for his livelihood. Such kind of freedom is provided in which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: Freedom of trade, occupation, or business is protected under Article 19(1)(g). It allows every citizen the right to practice any profession or carry on any occupation to earn a livelihood, subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of the general public.

questions.question: Poshan Abhiyaan is a programme to achieve the nutritional status of children from 0 to 6 years. Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for raising the nutrition level?
questions.solution: Article 47 directs the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health. Programmes like Poshan Abhiyaan are executive actions taken to fulfill this constitutional goal. Note: This article also suggests the prohibition of intoxicating drinks and harmful drugs.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution enshrines that if we are observing any religious procession, then we need to remember communal harmony?
questions.solution: Article 51A (e) is the fundamental duty to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all people of India, transcending religious and regional diversities. Observing communal harmony during religious processions is a direct application of this duty.

questions.question: In India, which of the following statements regarding Fundamental Duty is NOT correct?
questions.option_1: Article 51-A is related to Fundamental Duties
questions.option_2: Total number of Fundamental Duties are 11
questions.option_4: Incorporated in Part IV-A of the Constitution
questions.solution: The statement that Fundamental Duties were 'Inserted by 43rd Constitutional Amendment' is NOT correct. They were inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 based on the Swaran Singh Committee's report. Facts: They are in Part IV-A, Article 51A, and now total 11 in number.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the formation of New States and Alteration of Areas, Boundaries or names of existing States?
questions.solution: Article 3 authorizes Parliament to form new states and alter the areas, boundaries, or names of existing states. Requirement: A bill for this purpose can be introduced only with the prior recommendation of the President, who must refer the bill to the concerned state legislature for their views.

questions.question: While traveling in a train, one of the travelers started speaking against the Indian freedom struggle and noble ideals of it. Which of the following Articles mentions the fundamental duties in relation to such circumstances?
questions.solution: Article 51-A [b] is the fundamental duty to cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom. Speaking against these ideals contradicts this specific constitutional obligation.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution has the idea that ‘No child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment?
questions.solution: Article 24 explicitly prohibits the employment of children below 14 in any factory, mine, or hazardous employment. It is an absolute right intended to safeguard the health and childhood of citizens. Note: Non-hazardous work was previously allowed but is now largely restricted by the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution prohibits forced labour and prevents exploitation?
questions.solution: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and begar (forced labour) and other similar forms of forced labour. Any contravention of this provision is an offence punishable in accordance with the law. Context: It protects both citizens and non-citizens from exploitation by the state or private individuals.

questions.question: The Government of India is providing Ayushman Bharat Yojana, a health scheme. This type of government efforts falls under of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
questions.solution: Government efforts like Ayushman Bharat fall under Article 47, which mandates the State to improve public health as one of its primary duties. Goal: By providing health cover, the state moves toward fulfilling the Directive Principle of improving the standard of living.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles says that double jeopardy which says that “no person shall be prosecuted or punished for the same offence more than once.”?
questions.solution: Article 20 (2) provides the protection against Double Jeopardy, stating that no person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once. Scope: This protection is available only in proceedings before a court of law or a judicial tribunal; it does not apply to departmental or administrative inquiries.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Directive Principles of State Policy, a working woman on maternity leave, must receive all maternity benefits from the employer?
questions.solution: Under Article 42, the State must secure maternity relief for working women. This principle has been codified in laws like the Maternity Benefit Act, ensuring women receive paid leave and medical bonus. Note: It ensures that the biological necessity of motherhood does not lead to economic disadvantage.

questions.question: Which of the following article says that ‘It shall be the duty of every citizen of India who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years’?
questions.solution: Article 51A(k) is the 11th Fundamental Duty. It states that a parent or guardian must provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between 6 and 14 years. History: This was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, alongside the creation of the Fundamental Right to education (Art 21A).

questions.question: Article 22 of the Indian Constitution is related to which of the following?
questions.solution: Article 22 provides protection against arrest and detention, including specific safeguards for preventive detention (detaining a person without trial to prevent a future crime). Safe-guards: A person cannot be detained for more than 3 months unless an advisory board reports sufficient cause for extended detention.

questions.question: X and Y are working as managers in a restaurant but they receive unequal pay for the same work. Which Article of the Directive Principles of State Policy provides for equal pay for equal work?
questions.solution: Article 39(d) provides the Directive Principle of 'Equal pay for equal work' for both men and women. While it is a DPSP and not directly enforceable as a Fundamental Right, the courts have used it in conjunction with Articles 14 and 16 to ensure wage parity in public employment.

questions.question: Which of the following noble ideals is mentioned in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_1: Liberty of opportunity, economic, social, faith, and expression
questions.option_2: Liberty of expression, civil, political, worship, and belief
questions.option_3: Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship
questions.option_4: Liberty of belief, fiscal, personal, faith, and worship
questions.solution: The Preamble secures Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship to all citizens of India. Structure: These five types of liberty are essential for the individual development and the secular nature of the Indian polity.
